audit: OPSIQ Stage A7.5 — Systemic Invariant Verification & Architecture Hardening

findings.description: Actor identity written to privacy-control audit record comes from request body, not verified session. Any authenticated caller can forge the appliedBy field.
Same forgeable actor-ID pattern. appliedBy on retention policy record is caller-supplied.
Actor who recorded consent taken verbatim from request body. Authenticated caller can store arbitrary identity in consent record.
detectedBy is caller-supplied and stored in harm-event record. Authenticated user can attribute safety-critical records to any actor identity.

findings.evidence: const existing = await db.idempotencyRecord.findFirst({ where: { idempotencyKey } })
findings.description: Idempotency key lookup not scoped to workspaceId. Cross-tenant response leakage possible on key collision. Schema has no workspaceId column — requires DB migration to fix.
updateSyncJobStatus creates externalSyncJob with random ID on every call. No unique constraint, no upsert. Every retry appends a new row.
Same duplicate-creation risk on success path.

findings.evidence: const user = await db.user.create(...) [followed by 4 non-transactional creates]
findings.description: Signup creates 5 records in sequential non-transactional calls. Partial failure leaves user record without workspace/session, blocking future signup retries with 'Email already in use'.

findings.evidence: user = await db.user.create({ data: { id: randomUUID(), email: member.email ... } })
findings.description: Concurrent invitations for same email: both pass null-check (L56-58), both attempt user.create. Second throws unhandled P2002.
findUnique then create without transaction. Concurrent upgrade requests for same workspace: second throws P2002.
sequenceNumber computed outside $transaction. Concurrent calls both read N, both insert N+1. Unique constraint prevents corruption but gives unhandled P2002 to caller.
6 mutations across security-sensitive governed entities with zero audit coverage. No emitAuditEvent import, no tx.auditEvent.create anywhere in file.
3 operatorItem mutations without canonical audit. Embedded JSON auditTrail column (line 207-217) is a document field, NOT a system audit event. No emitAuditEvent import.
triggerReEvaluationOnCompletion writes outcomeDelta to governed decision without audit. No emitAuditEvent import in file.
linkDecisionToRecommendation updates decision-to-recommendation linkage without audit event. No emitAuditEvent import.
System-level projection rebuild writes recommendation without audit. Lower risk (infrastructure operation), but rebuild should emit a platform audit event.
Event projection handler updates recommendation read-model without audit. Upstream CanonicalEvent provides partial traceability but projection write is unaudited.
updateItem and applyOverride on OperatorItem (governed decision) use WHERE { id } only. No version guard. Last write silently wins on concurrent access.
recordDecisionOutcome uses WHERE { id } with no status or version guard. Sibling transitionDecisionState uses updateMany with status guard (line 106) — inconsistent.
3 operatorItem.update calls write impact, outcome, ROI fields with WHERE { id } only. Can race against state-transition writes.
outcomeDelta update on governed decision with WHERE { id, workspaceId } — no version guard.
Evaluation route writes to OperatorItem with WHERE { id, workspaceId } — no version. Concurrent state transition can interleave.
transitionActionState: version incremented in data but NOT in WHERE guard. TOCTOU: both concurrent callers pass read+validate, second write overwrites first.
updateAction: pre-checks version at line 462 then updates at 479 with no version in WHERE. Classic TOCTOU — should use updateMany with version in WHERE.

initializeInterventionState, transitionPhase, blockEngagement, unblockEngagement all do findUnique+update without version in WHERE. withVersionCheck helper exists and is used elsewhere but missed here.
updateRecommendationPriorityFromScore and updateRecommendation both have TOCTOU version races: pre-read without version in WHERE on update.
RecoveryAction has version column but WHERE is { id } only. No version guard on update.
OwnerBusiness has version column but WHERE is { id } only.

OwnerOperationsAction and 5 sibling tables (owner-sales, owner-finance, owner-marketing, owner-cashflow, owner-sop, owner-strategy action.service.ts) have no version column. CAS is architecturally impossible without schema migration.
Intake route creates governed decision with workspace membership check only. Canonical decisions/create route gates on CAPABILITIES.DECISION_CREATE. Intake bypasses capability entirely.
Required permission level for proof review taken from client request body (body.requiredPermission). Attacker can set any GuidedExecutionPermission value to downgrade authorization requirement.
'execute' not in hasPermission map for any role. Route permanently denies all users. Functional breakage.
'fail_decision' not in hasPermission map. Route permanently denies all users.
'verify_outcome' not in hasPermission map. Route permanently denies all users including admin.
'record_outcome' not in hasPermission map. Route permanently denies all users.

DEFAULT_MARGIN_FLOOR_PCT=15 (percent) divided by 100 inline to become 0..1 fraction for opportunity-contract-guardrails.ts. Same business rule encoded in two unit systems bridged by ad-hoc /100 conversion. Any new caller that misses this conversion silently applies floor 100× wrong.

Second margin floor (net, 5%) exists independently of DEFAULT_MARGIN_FLOOR_PCT=15 (gross). Different metrics — not a duplicate — but no cross-reference means policy changes must be applied to both independently.
